Respondent -----
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SUJIT NARAYAN PRASAD HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE NAVNEET KUMAR --------
For the Appellant : Mr. Durga, C. Mishra, Advocate For the State : Mrs. Anuradha Sahay, APP  --------
 th Order No. 07/ Dated: 11 December, 2024 IA No.12280 of 2024 1.

The instant Appeal has been listed for passing appropriate order on the instant Interlocutory Application filed on behalf of appellant under Section 430(1) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for suspension of sentence/grant of bail during the pendency of the instant Cr. Appeal (DB) No. 1449 of 2022 in connection with Special POCSO Case No.35 of 2020 + POCSO 35A of 2020 against the judgment of conviction dated 21.09.2022 and order of sentence dated 27.09.2022 passed by learned Special Judge (POCSO) Dumka, whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted under Sections 376(DA) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life and fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default of payment of fine,
further directed to undergo S.I. for six months for the offence under Section 376(DA) of IPC and further sentenced him to undergo R.I. for two years for the offence punishable under Section 506 of the IPC.

sentences.text: It has been contended on behalf of the appellant that if the testimony of the victim who has been examined as PW-1 will be taken into consideration in entirety then it would be evident that she has failed in proving the prosecution version.
It has further been submitted that the victim has not supported the entire story particularly the manner by which she was subjected to forceful physical relationship amounting to rape.
The contention has been raised that the issue of rape has not been found to be in corroboration by the doctor who was examined as PW-8.
It has further been submitted that PW-2 and PW-3, mother and father of the prosecutrix has also not supported the prosecution version.
It has been submitted that there is delay in instituting the F.I.R. that is of the period of 19 days.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant based upon the aforesaid grounds has submitted that it is a fit case where the sentence is to be suspended.

4. While on the other hand, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and has contended by referring the testimony of PW-1, the victim that she has fully supported the prosecution version.

The submission has been made that if there is any discrepancy regarding the manner of the commission of rape that will not be fatal reason being that the testimony of the victim since has supported in the present case regarding the commission of rape.
It has further been submitted that as per the medical evidence, the victim was minor and there is no challenge to the issue of age on behalf of the appellant.
Further submission has been made that it is incorrect on the part of the appellant to take the ground that the PW-2 and PW-3, the mother and father has not supported the prosecution version.
Further submission has been made that even if there is delay of 19 days in instituting the FIR, the same cannot be ground in view of the explanation made by PW-1 in para 19 of the testimony.
The learned State counsel based upon the aforesaid grounds has submitted that it is not a fit case where sentenced is to be suspended.

5. This Court has heard the learned counsel for the parties and gone across the findings recorded by learned trial Court in the impugned judgment passed as also the testimony and exhibits as available in the Lower Court Record.

6. This court in order to appreciate the argument advanced on behalf of the parties has gone through the testimony of PW-1, the victim, it is evident therefrom that she has supported the prosecution version in entirety and remained consistent in the cross-examination.

The question has been raised regarding the manner of commission of rape, which according to our 2 Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No. 1449 of 2022 considered view cannot be material and said to be fatal for the prosecution reason being that the manner is not to be seen at this stage, rather, the version of the prosecutrix victim is to be taken into consideration and herein the PW-1 has fully supported the prosecution version regarding the commission of rape upon her by the appellant.
So far as testimony of PW-2 and PW-3, mother and father of the prosecturix are concerned, they have also fully supported the prosecution version.
The question of delay of 19 days in instituting the FIR has been raised.
In her testimony the PW-1, in para 3 and 19 has assigned reason for delay in instituting the FIR.

2 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since, the judgment of conviction is based on the basis of the testimony of PW-1, victim who remained consistent in the cross- examination as also having supported by PW-2 & PW-3, therefore,
this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case where sentence is to be suspended.
8. As such, the Interlocutory Application stands rejected.
9. Accordingly, the instant interlocutory application being I.A. No.12280 of 2024 stands disposed of.

10. It is made clear that any observation made hereinabove will not prejudice the case on merit,
since, the criminal appeal is pending before this Court for its consideration.
